subject: bismarkCytosineReport data with mincov=0, - having problems with CpG destranding

messages.author: c02737bb0ac0a7f0
messages.subject: bismarkCytosineReport data with mincov=0, - having problems with CpG destranding
parts:
Hi,

I'm trying to load processed WGBS data into methylKit. My data are in "bismarkCytosineReport" format, and I'm using the "methRead" function from methylKit.
file.list2  <- list("test1.bed","test2.bed")

myobj.test2.cov1  <- methRead(file.list2, sample.id = list("s1","s2"), assembly = "hg19", pipeline = "bismarkCytosineReport", header=F, context = "CpG", treatment = c(0,1), mincov = 1)

In the next step, I'm using the unite(..., destrand =T) function, to merge the CpG data from both strands.
When I apply the setting mincov=1, all works fine with the caveat that, for positions where there is no coverage for one strand in one sample, I also lose the available information for other samples too.
> unite(myobj.test2.cov1, destrand = TRUE)
methylBase object with 13 rows
--------------
   chr start   end strand coverage1 numCs1 numTs1 coverage2 numCs2 numTs2
1 chr1 10469 10469      +         2      2      0         2      1      1
2 chr1 10471 10471      +         2      2      0         2      1      1
3 chr1 10484 10484      +         2      2      0         2      2      0
4 chr1 10488 10488      +         1      1      0         1      1      0
5 chr1 10489 10489      +         2      1      1         2      1      1
6 chr1 10493 10493      +         2      2      0         2      2      0


Then I tried to use mincov=0, but the unite(..., destrand =T) doesn't seem to work correctly in that situation:
> myobj.test2.cov0  <- methRead(file.list2, sample.id = list("s1","s2"), assembly = "hg19", pipeline = "bismarkCytosineReport", header=F, context = "CpG", treatment = c(0,1), mincov = 0)
> unite(myobj.test2.cov0, destrand = TRUE)
methylBase object with 20 rows
--------------
   chr start   end strand coverage1 numCs1 numTs1 coverage2 numCs2 numTs2
1 chr1 10468 10468      +         0      0      0         1      0      1
2 chr1 10469 10469      +         2      2      0         2      1      1
3 chr1 10470 10470      +         0      0      0         1      0      1
4 chr1 10471 10471      +         2      2      0         2      1      1
5 chr1 10483 10483      +         0      0      0         1      0      1
6 chr1 10484 10484      +         2      2      0         2      2      0
As you see, the reads from the two strands don't get merged, and also the start/end position of the + and - cytosines seems off.

To summarize, I'm trying to always preserve the read number information from both strands, even in situations where some samples only have coverage from one of the strands.
Is there a way to achieve that in methylKit? Am I missing something here?

R 3.3.1
methylKit 0.99.2 (I tried both the latest stable version, and the development version)
data.table 1.9.6

The heads  of the data files:
>head test1.bed
chr1    10469    +    2    0    CG    CGC

>head test2.bed

messages.author: ab8277113f65c05e
messages.subject: Re: [methylkit_discussion] bismarkCytosineReport data with mincov=0, - having problems with CpG destranding
parts:
Hi Alex,
There is no way to achieve that in methylKit easily. if you have cytosine report files that have CpGs with 0 coverage, you can fool the unite() function not to drop CpGs that do not have coverage in the samples.

You can also do the same thing by adding rows to one of the methylRaw objects in your environment. The rows should have CpG coordinates that are not covered and their coverage,numCs and numTs should be 0. 

Best,
Altuna
